summary.title: Alignment review: unchanged release handoff
summary.detail: A read-only view of release intent, evidence, uncertainty, and the human-owned approval boundary before Superpowers planning.

goals.title: Verified release intent
goals.detail: Expose scope, evidence, operational responsibility, and unresolved risk before implementation planning.

goals.title: Human-owned decision
goals.detail: Only an explicit current stakeholder message can authorize the exact reviewed snapshot.

evidence.excerpt: The manifest identifies Approved Release Handoff and lists the exact human-authored files protected by the reviewed snapshot.
The release dossier must expose intent, evidence, responsibility, and unresolved risk before implementation brainstorming begins.
The goals are verified release intent and a human-owned decision on the unchanged presented dossier.
The release sponsor has decision authority for the presented dossier and its acknowledged limitations.
The service operator needs visible rollback ownership and operational risk rather than a false completeness claim.
The sponsor reviews canonical evidence and findings; only an explicit decision on the unchanged issuance can unlock handoff.
A current explicit human approval produces a matching handoff only while issued, rendered, approved, and current snapshots remain identical.
Changing any included dossier file after approval makes the decision stale and blocks handoff until a new review.
Epistemic Alignment presents evidence to the sponsor and passes only a verified dossier to Superpowers for downstream brainstorming.
Canonical dossier artifacts carry semantic meaning; the derived Site and thin helper have presentation and integrity responsibilities only.
The thin gate hashes included paths and checks freshness without judging requirements, BDD, C4, or consensus.
Approval stays in the host conversation; the review Site remains read-only and cannot impersonate a stakeholder decision.
The sponsor is assumed able to inspect the local review surface in the current interaction; public hosting is not required.
Reviewer labels are descriptive rather than authenticated; regulated or quorum workflows require an external identity/signature system.

stakeholders.title: Release sponsor

stakeholders.title: Service operator
stakeholders.detail: Needs visible rollback ownership and risk rather than a false semantic certificate.

useCases.title: Approve an unchanged release handoff
useCases.detail: The sponsor reviews canonical evidence and the exact digest; only an unchanged approved snapshot reaches Superpowers.

behavior.title: Explicit approval of the unchanged snapshot
behavior.detail: Given the findings and digest are visible, a current human approval unlocks a matching handoff only while files remain unchanged.

behavior.title: Post-approval edit blocks handoff
behavior.detail: Any included-file change makes the approval stale and requires a new presentation and decision.
